titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 2/2008 (ވަޒީފާއާބެހޭ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Employment Act (Law 2/2008) to change the rules for foreigners working in the Maldives. It rewrites Article 65 so that foreigners may work only after getting a work permit, and rewrites Article 65-1 so that the number of foreign workers, including the maximum from any one country, is set by regulation after a labour-market assessment and advice from the Cabinet. It adds new Articles 65-2 to 65-8: employers must register the worksite, get a quota and get a work permit before bringing in a foreign worker, and the bill sets fees, inspections and fines. It also adds Article 66-1 naming the ministry in charge of foreign workers, and changes Article 96 so that ministry writes the related regulations.
whyItMatters: Employers who bring in foreign workers would need a registered worksite, a quota and a work permit for each worker, with fixed fees and fines of up to MVR 100,000. Employers who neglect their foreign workers, for example by not paying wages, could be fined MVR 50,000 per worker and publicly named.
keyProvisions: Article 65: foreigners may work in the Maldives only after getting a work permit, and working without one is banned. Exempt groups include people with diplomatic immunity, staff of international organisations or people seconded under international agreements, holders of visas other than a work visa under the Immigration Act (Law 1/2007), and others exempted by another law.

Article 65-1: the fixed cap of 100,000 workers from any one country is replaced. Yearly numbers, sectors and per-country limits are set by regulation after a labour-market assessment and on Cabinet advice. Where numbers exceed a limit, steps to reduce them must follow reasonable notice, and any deadline may not exceed 36 months.

Articles 65-2 and 65-3: before bringing in a foreign worker, an employer must register the worksite, get a quota and get a work permit. Foreign workers may work only at registered worksites, and registrations can be cancelled.

Articles 65-4 and 65-5: the quota fee is MVR 2,000 a year and the work permit fee is MVR 350 a month. Fees can be reviewed on a cycle set in regulations (the text mentions three years and at least 18 months), and each review may raise a fee by no more than 30%. Employers must also keep a security deposit with the ministry.

Article 65-6: ministry inspectors may enter worksites suspected of illegal foreign labour, with or without notice, question people and copy records. Homes need the owner's permission or a court order. If a breach is proved, the ministry can stop the business, close the worksite, refer workers to immigration, deport them, or cancel the employer's permit.

Articles 65-7 and 65-8: an employer who neglects foreign workers (unpaid wages, unmet basic duties, illegal agency services, or moving a worker to another job without their knowledge) can be named publicly and fined MVR 50,000 per worker, with permits suspended for repeat cases. Other breaches carry fines of up to MVR 100,000. Regulations must be published within 3 months of the law taking effect.
whoIsAffected: Employers and businesses that bring in foreign workers, foreign workers in the Maldives, and the ministry responsible for foreign employment.
statedReasons: The government says the bill is meant to address foreigners working illegally in the Maldives by revising the Employment Act's rules on foreign employment and strengthening enforcement of the law.
